newsitem.title: USA: Lili still a hurricane as it spins east of Bermuda.
newsitem.headline: Lili still a hurricane as it spins east of Bermuda.

text.p: Lili maintained its minimal hurricane strength Tuesday as it spun in the open Atlantic east of Bermuda, but was no threat to any land, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), the center of Hurricane Lili was near latitude 33.3 north and longitude 53.5 west, or about 645 miles (1,035 km) east of Bermuda and moving east-southeast near 10 mph (16 kph).
Lili's maximum sustained winds were near 75 mph (120 kph), but it was expected to lose strength within the next day or so.

Lili had bypassed Bermuda on Sunday, sparing the British colony the worst of its winds and rain, after a rampage that began last week off the coast of Central America. Flooding from the storm was blamed for 10 deaths in Nicaragua, Honduras and Costa Rica before it moved north over Cuba and then east through the central Bahamas.
